approval_source.question_set: How to handle the five attack types the node does not refuse (T4 staking, governance and root-control families)

reason: Building the T4 root-control attack family, a source read found that the node admitted a kit replacement control in any JSON encoding: it decoded the bytes and re-encoded them, where the emergency, upgrade (v1 and v2) and handover controls, and the kit replacement's own receipt, refuse bytes that are not their canonical encoding. Whoever saw a signed replacement could send it again under other transaction hashes. It could still take effect only once (one replacement per block; its sequence is the epoch it creates), and nobody could make one without three upgrade keys, so the effect was duplicate mempool entries and hashes, not a second replacement.

decisions.question: Non-canonical kit replacement
decisions.rule: A kit replacement control is admitted only as its canonical JSON (the bytes serde_json writes for it), as the other root controls are; any other encoding of the same control is not a kit replacement at all, so admission refuses it as an invalid transaction, as it refuses the other root controls' non-canonical bytes (the decoder's own error is "Kit replacement record is not canonical"). The release tools already write canonical bytes, so no honest control changes. The T4 root-control family counts a re-encoded control as refused only when admission refuses it.

does_not_authorize: any change to who may sign a replacement, its notice or its scope (P01, 8 October 2026)
